preRegisteredBefore: any measurement at 1M nodes, and before the span implementation exists
note: Transcribed from the approved Phase 4 plan. These are the values the author was willing to be held to in advance. Moving a number in this file after seeing a result invalidates the experiment, and the git history is the evidence that it was not done.

scale.rule: the baseline must satisfy every threshold on every shape to trigger REVERSE

baselineMustSatisfy.rationale: one-time cost behind a loading state, so generous
must leave the rest of a 16.7ms frame for the renderer
same frame argument; this is the live-update path M2 depends on
called up to a few hundred times per frame
baselineMustSatisfy.caveat: timed in batches of 1000, so this is a batch p99 divided by the batch size, not a true per-call p99

heap.rationale: projection overhead should not dominate the data it projects

spanMustImproveBreachedMetricsBy.rationale: a 20% win does not pay for a second data structure, its invariants and its bugs

spanRegressionMustBeReported.rationale: faster at restructuring and slower at reading is a trade-off, not an improvement, and must appear in the README next to the wins

shapeClassification.rationale: breaches confined to pathological shapes produce NARROW rather than CONFIRM

outcomes.REVERSE: baseline satisfies every threshold on every shape; the span tree is never written and ADR-0002 is withdrawn
outcomes.CONFIRM: baseline breaches on the majority of shapes and the span tree improves each breached metric by at least 3x at p99
outcomes.NARROW: breaches confined to pathological shapes; the span tree ships and the materialized projection stays as a documented selectable mode
